answer: A farm's weakness is that its names behave alike. Let the registry compare accounts by when they act, which counterparties they pick and how their wording drifts, then pool any tight cluster into one payout share. A real sonnet writer and a harbor pilot never ripple in step, so the farm must run each fake on separate schedules, partners and styles, which costs a separate operator's attention per name. Merged clusters pay one share, so extra names only add upkeep.
